neighbours.label: the adjective/adverb right after intensifier 'so' heading a result clause (so real that..., so much so)
fire: The noise was so loud that the neighbors called the police.
Her painting looked so lifelike that visitors tried to touch it.
The fans were so excited, the stadium shook for an hour.
The recipe is so simple that a child could follow it.
The storm was fierce. So fierce, in fact, that schools closed for days.
The hike was so steep that half the group turned back.
Prices rose so quickly that stores changed labels twice a day.
The film was popular, so much so that theaters added late shows.
quiet: The noise was loud and the neighbors called the police.
Her painting looked lifelike, and visitors tried to touch it.
The fans were excited, and the stadium shook for an hour.
The recipe is simple and a child could follow it.
The storm was fierce. Schools in the region closed for days.
The hike was steep, and half the group turned back.
Prices rose quickly, and stores changed labels twice a day.
The film was popular, and theaters added late shows.
